content.title: About
content.content: Tap water is drinking water supplied by municipal water systems. It undergoes treatment and disinfection to meet safety standards and be suitable for everyday consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In most countries tap water undergoes triple treatment: mechanical, chemical and biological.
Some regions add fluoride to tap water to help prevent cavities.
Mineral content (hardness) varies according to the geology of the area the water passes through.
Tap water is typically 30‑50 times cheaper than bottled water.
In many places tap water can be used for cooking without additional filtration.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Regular consumption of clean water maintains the body’s fluid balance, essential for all physiological processes.

items.title: Kidney function support
items.content: Adequate water intake helps flush metabolic waste and reduces the risk of kidney stone formation.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Water participates in breaking down food and facilitates nutrient absorption.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Proper hydration contributes to skin elasticity and overall appearance.

items.title: Body temperature regulation
items.content: Sweating and evaporation of water help keep body temperature within a safe range.

items.title: Contamination
items.content: In some areas tap water may contain heavy metals, bacteria or chemical pollutants; it is advisable to check water quality.

items.title: Water hardness
items.content: High mineral levels can cause scale buildup on appliances and may lead to dry skin.

items.title: Chlorine and by‑products
items.content: Chlorine is commonly used for disinfection and can impart taste and cause irritation in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tap water can be consumed directly, after boiling, or filtered if quality is uncertain. It is also used for preparing beverages, meals, and household purposes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store water in a clean, sealed container, preferably glass or food‑grade plastic, in a cool place. For prolonged storage, replace the water every 2‑3 days.
